title: How I Cut a Brand Film in 48 Hours, Without Losing the Story
excerpt: A tight deadline is not an excuse for a sloppy edit. Here's the exact workflow I use to turn raw footage into a finished brand film in two days.
body:
Every editor knows the panic: the client calls on Monday and the film is due Wednesday. Over the years I've delivered more tight turnaround edits than I can count, and the difference between panic and process is a system. Here's mine.

Hour 0, 4: Watch everything once, at speed

Before touching the timeline, I watch all footage at 1.5, 2x speed with a notepad open. I'm not picking clips yet, I'm finding moments: the look, the laugh, the turn of phrase that becomes the spine of the story.

Hour 4, 8: Build the spine first

I cut the narrative arc before any B roll: interview best lines, key actions, the emotional beat. If the spine works in silence, the film will work with polish. If it doesn't, no color grade will save it.

Cut the story first, the beauty second. Never the other way around.

Hour 8, 24: The assembly

B roll, music, pacing. I build a rhythm that matches the brand's energy, fast cuts for product energy, long breaths for NGO storytelling. Captions and titles go in early so the client reviews a near final cut, not a rough sketch.

Hour 24, 44: Polish rounds

Color grade, sound balance, sound design details, export checks for every platform (16:9 master, 9:16 reels, 1:1 squares). One structured feedback round with the client, with time stamped notes, not vague feelings.

Hour 44, 48: Deliver

Files named properly, delivered in folders the client actually understands: web / social / print ready. Because a great edit that arrives as chaos isn't finished.
